input_signals.name: Inventory Margin Divergence
input_signals.hypothesis: Rapid inventory accumulation combined with deteriorating gross margins predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Inventory growth is particularly concerning when firms are losing pricing power or facing rising production costs. The joint signal targets potentially unproductive stock accumulation rather than inventory investment associated with healthy margins.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( growth( invt, 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Distress-Financed Equity Issuance
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance predicts lower returns when the issuing firm has persistently negative operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: External equity raised during a cash-flow shortfall is more likely to fund fragile expansion or ongoing operating deficits than high-return investment. The zero cash-flow threshold creates a direct quality condition, leaving issuance by internally healthy firms unpenalized.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), indicator( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Financed Capex Gap
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt raised to support capital expenditure that exceeds internal operating cash flow predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The funding-gap condition distinguishes capex that cannot be covered internally, while debt growth relative to capex directly measures reliance on external borrowing rather than an ambiguous static leverage tilt. Winsorization reduces the influence of firms with unusually small capex denominators without weakening the financing-source mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), capx ), 1 ), indicator( sub( capx, oancf ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Capital Replacement Discipline
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose capital expenditure remains close to the depreciation-implied replacement need earn higher returns than firms exhibiting extreme underinvestment or expansion.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the archived incremental-cash-payoff mechanism and instead measures investment discipline relative to consumed capital. The normalized absolute gap is bounded and symmetric, penalizing both aggressive expansion beyond replacement needs and potential undermaintenance without requiring a long history or unstable payoff denominator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: neg( abs( ratio( sub( capx, dp ), add( capx, dp ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fragility-Weighted Replacement Imbalance
input_signals.expression: NEG(MUL(ABS(RATIO(SUB(capx, dp), ADD(capx, dp))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Large deviations from replacement-level capital spending predict lower returns primarily among firms with weak accumulated profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier symmetric replacement signal had an exceptionally strong cross-sectional slope but negligible FF5 alpha, plausibly because its short portfolio pooled financially strong and fragile firms. Weighting the bounded replacement gap by retained-earnings weakness concentrates the low-signal tail in firms where either overexpansion or undermaintenance is least sustainable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: neg( mul( abs( ratio( sub( capx, dp ), add( capx, dp ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capacity-Weighted Margin Realization
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross-margin erosion predicts lower returns more strongly when it follows a large fixed-capacity expansion.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the binary builder indicator with lagged investment magnitude removes the zero-valued mass in the prior post-build signal. The signed industry-standardized margin outcome places successful large builders in the low-signal tail and unsuccessful large builders in the high-signal tail, improving the economic interpretation of the spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( growth( ppent, 1 ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory Turnover Decay
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms experiencing a persistent increase in inventory relative to realized product throughput earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Inventory divided by cost of goods sold measures the stock committed per unit of operating throughput, so an upward trend indicates slowing turnover and rising obsolescence or markdown risk. This abandons the inventory-adjusted working-capital difference and its accrual-sign ambiguity, while retaining continuous coverage without an indicator-generated zero mass.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( trend( ratio( invt, cogs ), 3 ) )

input_signals.name: Workforce Gross-Profit Productivity
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating more gross profit per employee earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic timing change with a distinct unit-economics mechanism that measures the output quality of the existing labor investment. Gross profit per employee distinguishes productive labor capacity from costly workforce intensity without relying on persistent employment-growth ranks, and industry ranking reduces structural differences in labor intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), emp ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Workforce Cash Productivity
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating more operating cash flow per employee earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross profit per employee produced strong and consistent evidence, but it does not verify that labor output converts into cash after overhead and working-capital needs. This cash-based unit-productivity measure tests that distinct quality channel without relying on hiring rates, temporal gates, or sparse observations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oancf, emp ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cumulative Investment Profit Backing
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with greater accumulated retained earnings relative to their physical and inventory investment stock earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the weak capacity-weighted profitability-change template and asks whether the existing operating investment base has generated cumulative profits over the firm's history. Combining net fixed assets and inventory captures both long-lived and working-capital commitments, while the signed retained-earnings numerator distinguishes validated investment from expansion associated with accumulated losses.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( re, add( ppent, invt ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Term-Funded Capacity Growth
input_signals.hypothesis: Fixed-capacity growth accompanied by increasing current liabilities predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This directly measures the contemporaneous co-movement of long-lived investment and short-term funding rather than inferring mismatch from a potentially negative permanent-capital denominator. Signed current-liability growth places capacity builders that reduce short-term obligations opposite builders that expand them, producing continuous and economically distinct portfolio tails.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( growth( ppent, 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( lct, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory Cash Productivity
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating more operating cash flow per dollar of inventory investment earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the sparse acquisition-only design and its non-acquirer ranking problem with a broadly observable investment-productivity mechanism. Cash flow per unit of inventory distinguishes productive working-capital deployment from inventory that absorbs funding without supporting cash generation, while industry ranking controls for normal turnover differences.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oancf, invt ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory Turnover Recovery
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose current inventory turnover is close to its recent firm-specific peak earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The strong turnover-decay result indicates that deterioration in inventory throughput is informative, but a linear trend may be sensitive to a single old observation. Distance from the recent turnover maximum measures whether inventory efficiency has recovered or remains impaired while controlling for each firm's normal turnover level.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( ratio( cogs, invt ), ts_max( ratio( cogs, invt ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-Validated Capital Payoff
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(sale, 1), LAG(ADD(capx, dp), 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oancf, 1), LAG(ADD(capx, dp), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Prior capital commitments predict higher returns when followed by both incremental sales and incremental operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales-based capex productivity generated strong portfolio alpha but an opposing Fama-MacBeth slope, whereas the cash-payoff version produced moderately consistent evidence. Requiring both outcomes prevents sales expansion without cash realization from entering the high-signal tail, and capex plus depreciation provides a more stable one-period capital denominator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( delta( sale, 1 ), lag( add( capx, dp ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( delta( oancf, 1 ), lag( add( capx, dp ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Share-Funded Capacity Growth
input_signals.hypothesis: Fixed-capacity growth accompanied by a rising share of interest-bearing short-term debt in current liabilities predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier current-liability funding signal had a strong negative cross-sectional slope but positive FF5 alpha, potentially because trade credit and other operating liabilities can accompany healthy expansion. Focusing on a shift toward short-term debt isolates refinancing-dependent capacity growth, while the signed debt-share change places deleveraging builders in the opposite portfolio tail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( growth( ppent, 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( delta( ratio( dlc, lct ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Conversion-Weighted Labor Productivity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, SUB(sale, cogs)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profit per employee predicts higher returns when that operating output converts efficiently into cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The second component is cash conversion of gross profit and does not share the employee denominator, making it economically distinct from the labor-productivity level. Signed industry standardization places productive firms with poor cash conversion in the low-signal tail and avoids the coverage-degrading MIN bottleneck.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), emp ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oancf, sub( sale, cogs ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin-Risk Labor Rigidity
input_signals.hypothesis: Labor-intensive firms with unstable gross margins earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces profitability-per-worker and conversion-ratio recombinations with an operating-leverage mechanism. A large workforce per unit of sales is a more consequential commitment when unit margins are unstable, and industry ranking limits structural differences in labor intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( emp, sale ) ), ind_rank( vol( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fixed-Capital Cash Surplus
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating greater operating cash flow after capital consumption per dollar of installed gross fixed assets earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the repeated capacity-growth-times-funding-change template and measures the realized economic surplus of the installed capital stock. Subtracting depreciation distinguishes cash generation that merely offsets capital consumption from cash returns that represent productive capacity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), ppegt ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Productive Replacement Discipline
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(capx, dp), ADD(capx, dp))))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), ppegt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Replacement-level capital spending predicts higher returns when the installed fixed-capital stock also generates cash flow beyond capital consumption.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacement discipline had exceptional cross-sectional evidence but negligible alpha, while fixed-capital cash surplus produced consistent slope and portfolio evidence. Their interaction distinguishes disciplined maintenance of productive assets from mechanically balanced spending on low-return capacity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( abs( ratio( sub( capx, dp ), add( capx, dp ) ) ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), ppegt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt Unproductive-Capital Burden
input_signals.hypothesis: Low cash surplus from installed fixed assets combined with heavy short-term-debt reliance predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Poorly productive fixed capital becomes especially fragile when a large share of current liabilities is interest-bearing debt that must be refinanced. The interaction links realized capital quality to funding maturity without relying on investment-growth or debt-issuance anomalies.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( neg( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), ppegt ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dlc, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory Gross Return
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating greater gross profit per dollar committed to inventory earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces another inventory-growth–margin-deterioration interaction with a direct economic return on inventory investment. Gross profit per inventory dollar combines realized throughput and margin economics in one productivity measure, without recycling the archived margin trend or drawdown channels.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), invt ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Stress-Adjusted Workforce Gross Profit
input_signals.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), MUL(sale, SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3)))), emp), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating high gross profit per employee after charging for their recent margin drawdown earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The margin drawdown is converted into a dollar stress charge using current sales before calculating workforce productivity. This creates an integrated downside-adjusted unit-economics measure rather than mechanically blending archived productivity and labor-risk ranks.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), mul( sale, sub( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 3 ), ts_min( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) ), emp ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Conservative Inventory Gross Return
input_signals.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), invt), 3), VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), invt), 3)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high and stable gross profit per dollar of inventory earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Current inventory gross return produced strong joint evidence, but a single-period ratio can reflect temporary pricing or inventory liquidation. Subtracting volatility from the rolling mean estimates a conservative inventory payoff without the near-zero volatility denominator of a mean-to-volatility ratio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( sub( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), invt ), 3 ), vol( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), invt ), 3 ) ), 1 ) )
